cells.tense: Right now you're holding two readings of the thing at once, and you're in no hurry to pick.
cells.verb: Weighing what you know before you say it
cells.place: Where you point your attention and what you decide it's for
cells.ask: Offer the one clear next move you'd make if you had to name it, then let the structure you've set carry people without you standing over it — and let the order you made keep making sense to whoever steps into it.
cells.core: Right now you're holding two readings of the thing at once, and you're in no hurry to pick between them. People watching might read the pause as indecision, but it isn't — it's the quiet where the right answer lands on its own before you've argued it into place, and you know the difference. Because you've actually weighed it, the direction you set holds its weight. You called something, and it stands.
cells.sheetLine: You weigh it before you say it, and the direction you set holds.

cells.tense: You're already standing in the version of this where you had the answer before anyone asked — and it hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: Weighing what you know before you say it, so far ahead of the saying that the answer arrives demanded instead of offered
cells.place: Where you point your attention and what you decide it's for
cells.ask: Take the next step before the outcome is guaranteed, and keep taking it — direction returns the moment you stay in it past the first disappointment, and the shine comes back because what you've been building actually ripens, not because you held it up to the light.
cells.core: You're already living in the version of this where you had the answer before anyone asked, and that version hasn't happened. So you keep holding, keep waiting for the right moment, keep running the outcome in your head — and the deliberating has stopped serving the decision. You're bracing so hard for a future you can't write in that the present never gets your actual move. Knowing, overworked, becomes the thing that keeps you from acting on what you know.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the answer long past the moment that asked for it.

cells.tense: Somewhere behind you it stopped being safe to know what you know, and you've been standing at that door since.
cells.verb: Weighing what you know — and declining to let it reach a direction
cells.place: Where you point your attention and what you decide it's for
cells.ask: Let something you've actually lived through finish turning into an image of what you want next, and trust the picture when it comes — direction charges back through the deciding the moment what you've already digested is allowed to become what you're dreaming toward.
cells.core: Somewhere behind you it stopped being safe to know what you know, and you've stayed at that door: when the moment came, you kept the truth off the table instead of setting a direction with it. So decisions get deferred, options stay open, and 'not yet' does the job of 'this, not that.' The inner knowing didn't turn off — you did — and a direction you'll never point at is just the thought staying dark.
cells.sheetLine: You know something, and you've stopped letting it choose anything.

cells.tense: You're already steering by a read of this that turned out right — and you tell the story like it was the situation's doing.
cells.verb: Weighing what you know before you say it, without owning that you're the one weighing
cells.place: Where you point your attention and what you decide it's for
cells.ask: Say out loud what you gave and what you need back, once, plainly — fairness returns the moment exchange is allowed to be give-and-take instead of the running account you keep in your head.
cells.core: You're already steering by a read of the situation that turned out right — you picked the direction before you'd admit you were reading anything, and it landed. But you tell it like the situation decided, like you were just following what was there. The reading is doing the work; only the claim on it is missing. What you keep calling gut instinct or the obvious thing is yours, and it's been right often enough that you owe it the name.
cells.sheetLine: Your read has been steering this. You keep calling it the situation.
